brief: Small, luminous particles appear suspended, continuously orbiting a fixed central point. These particles trace smooth, colorful paths in closed loops, visually demonstrating the concept of centripetal force. The movement is stable by default, but the viewer can influence the system by dragging the mouse across the canvas. This action changes the perceived magnitude of the orbital force, causing the orbiting particles to spiral outward or pull tighter toward the center.
statement: This sketch visualizes centripetal force through a system of glowing particles that orbit a central point. The particles move in smooth, closed loops, demonstrating how force constantly pulls them toward the center while their momentum keeps them in motion. When the viewer drags their mouse across the canvas, they alter the perceived strength of this force — particles spiral outward or tighten their orbits accordingly. The system is stable by default but responsive to interaction, creating a tangible representation of physics principles through visual movement.
